column4: Visit note | 2025-09-08 04:30 PM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Anika Miah, 20, female. Ms. Miah consults because she suffers from severe menstrual cramps accompanied by bothersome nausea, which forces her to miss work or classes during her period. She works as a freelance photographer and mentions that her symptoms have become noticeably worse since a stressful family move to Khulna. She has a known history of Essential hypertension. She denies abnormal bleeding between periods, dizziness, or fever. Examination reveals a pain score 6/10, with other vitals recorded as BP 152/96 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, and weight 57 kg. Her abdomen is soft and non-tender on superficial palpation. Assessment: Primary dysmenorrhoea. Plan: a prescription was issued today. She was advised to use a hot water bottle for relief, do light exercise, and keep a detailed period diary. Follow-up in 3 months with the period diary.
